Load required packages:
```{r, message=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(misty)
library(rstatix)
library(knitr)
library(sjPlot)
library(Rmisc)
```
Import processed data.
```{r}
dat <- read.csv2('Data/Study3_data_processed.csv')
```

# Sample descriptives

*Note that the following demographic variables were removed from the data sets, to guarantee anonymity: Gender, age, educational background.*

```{r, echo=FALSE}
dat %>%
  summarise(mean = mean(BMI, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd = sd(BMI, na.rm = TRUE),
            min = min(BMI, na.rm = TRUE),
            max = max(BMI, na.rm = TRUE)
            ) %>%
  kable(format = 'markdown', digits = 2, 
        col.names = c('Mean BMI', 'Std. Dev.(BMI)', 'Min.(BMI)', 'Max.(BMI)'),
        caption = 'Body mass index')

```

We additionally assessed participants' eating style.

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Turn the eating style variable into a factor and add labels
dat <-
  dat %>% 
  mutate(nutrition = factor(nutri,
                           levels = c('1', '2', '3', '4', '5'),
                           labels = c('Unrestricted', 'Pescetarian', 'Vegetarian', 'Vegan', 'Other'))
         )
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
dat %>%
  count('nutrition') %>% 
  mutate(prop = prop.table(freq)*100) %>% 
  kable(format = 'markdown', digits = 2, col.names = c('Eating style', 'N', '%'))
```

The majority of participants followed either an unrestricted or vegetarian diet, a considerable number of participants was vegan or followed another diet.

# Control analyses

In these analyses, we checked whether the results of the main analyses remain stable when controlling for the causal belief in a health-taste relationship (`causal_HT`).

Also, participants tasted smoothies from a black and white box. We randomised the colours of the box with many tasty and not tasty foods, respectively. The variable `random_color` indicates which box had which colour. 

To check whether these variables affected the results, we ran the analyses again (for details, see R markdown file `Study3_analyses.Rmd`), while including causal health-taste belief as a covariate and randomisation of box colours as a factor.

```{r, include=FALSE}
# Turn the id and condition variable into factors and add labels.
dat <-
  dat %>% 
  mutate(id = factor(id),
         condition = factor(condition, 
                            levels = c('1', '2'), 
                            labels = c('Harmonious', 'Conflicting')),
         random_color = factor(random_color, 
                               levels = c('1', '2'), 
                               labels = c('Context 1 black, context 2 white', 'Context 1 white, context 2 black')),
         choice = factor(choice, 
                         levels = c('1', '2'), 
                         labels = c('Healthy food', 'Unhealthy food'))
  )
```

## Descriptive statistics of the covariate

```{r, echo=FALSE}
dat %>%
  summarise(mean = mean(causal_HT, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd = sd(causal_HT, na.rm = TRUE),
            min = min(causal_HT, na.rm = TRUE),
            max = max(causal_HT, na.rm = TRUE)
            ) %>%
  kable(format = 'markdown', digits = 2, 
        col.names = c('Mean belief', 'Std. Dev.(belief)', 'Min.(belief)', 'Max.(belief)'),
        caption = 'Belief in a causal health-taste relationship')
```

## Perceived health-taste relationship within contexts

```{r, include=FALSE}
# Restructure data into long format for the mixed ANOVA, convert the context variable into a factor.
dat_long_belief <-
  dat %>% 
  select(id, condition, belief_ht_c1_R, belief_ht_c2_R, random_color, causal_HT) %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = c('belief_ht_c1_R', 'belief_ht_c2_R'), 
               names_to = 'context',
               values_to = 'ht_rel') %>% 
  mutate(context = rec(context, '"belief_ht_c1_R" = 1; "belief_ht_c2_R" = 2')) %>%
  mutate(context = factor(context,
                          levels = c('1', '2'),
                          labels= c('1st context', '2nd context')))
```

### ANCOVA

```{r}
acv_ht_rel <- 
  dat_long_belief %>% 
  anova_test(dv = ht_rel, wid = id,
             between = c('condition', 'random_color'), 
             within = context,
             covariate = causal_HT,
             type = 3, 
             effect.size = 'pes')
```
```{r, echo=FALSE}
colnames(acv_ht_rel) <- c('Effect','df/nominator', 'df/denominator', '$F$', '$p$', 'Sig.', 'partial $\\eta^2$')
rownames(acv_ht_rel) <- c('Causal health-taste belief', 'Base rate manipulation', 'Colour randomisation', 'Context', 'Base rate manipulation*Colour randomisation', 'Causal health-taste belief*Context', 'Base rate manipulation*Context', 'Colour randomisation*Context', 'Base rate manipulation\\*Colour randomisation*Context')

kable(acv_ht_rel[-1], format = 'markdown',  digits = 2,
      caption = 'Results of the ANCOVA testing the effect of base rate manipulation and context on the perceived health-taste relationship')
```

## Perceived health-taste relationship across contexts

### ANCOVA

```{r}
acv_ht_rel_ov <-
  anova_test(
    data = dat, dv = belief_ht_overall_R,
    between = c(condition, random_color), 
    covariate = causal_HT,
    type = 3, 
    effect.size = 'pes')
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
colnames(acv_ht_rel_ov) <- c('Effect','df/nominator', 'df/denominator', '$F$', '$p$', 'Sig.', 'partial $\\eta^2$')
rownames(acv_ht_rel_ov) <- c('Causal health-taste belief', 'Base rate manipulation', 'Colour randomisation', 'Base rate manipulation*Colour randomisation')

kable(acv_ht_rel_ov[-1], format = 'markdown',  digits = 2)
```

## Choice for healthy smoothie

```{r}
lm_choice <- glm(formula = choice ~ condition + causal_HT + random_color, family= 'binomial', data = dat)
```

```{r, include=FALSE}
exp(cbind(OR = coef(lm_choice), confint(lm_choice)))
```

```{r, message=FALSE, echo=FALSE}
tab_model(lm_choice, show.est = T, show.se = T, show.stat = T, pred.labels = c('(Intercept)', 'Base rate manipulation', 'Causal health-taste belief', 'Colour randomisation'), dv.labels = 'Choice for healthy smoothie')
```

## Summary

The results remained stable when controlling for the belief in a causal health-taste relationship and the randomisation of context colours. Neither the causal health-taste belief, nor the randomisation affected the outcome variables in any way.
